personas.label: small-team_low-ops
personas.public_initial_context: The existing web service needs configurable read caching while preserving compatibility.
personas.hidden_summary: A three-person team running one regional instance wants a reversible cache without a new always-on service.

preference_nodes.criterion: May the implementation require a new long-running cache service?
preference_nodes.value: No. The default deployment must not add a new external always-on service.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: We cannot add a new always-on service. Please keep the default deployment self-contained.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Select an in-process or existing-database-assisted backend; external backends may only be optional adapters.
acceptable_alternatives: optional Redis adapter disabled by default
must_not: require Redis or another new service in the default path

preference_nodes.criterion: What deployment topology and coherence are required?
preference_nodes.value: Single regional process today; brief TTL-bounded staleness is acceptable after writes.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: It is a single regional process today. A short, documented TTL-bounded stale window is acceptable.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Use local invalidation plus conservative TTL rather than cross-process coherence machinery.
must_hold: no stale data beyond documented bound
must_not: claim cross-instance consistency that is not implemented

preference_nodes.criterion: What traffic and latency objective should drive complexity?
preference_nodes.value: Typical load is 40-60 RPS; prioritize predictability and simplicity over the last few milliseconds.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: We usually see 40-60 RPS. Predictability and maintainability matter more than shaving the last few milliseconds.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Avoid distributed coordination and tune bounded cache size/TTL for modest traffic.
acceptable_alternatives: TTL cache with single-flight per process
must_hold: cache stampede protection proportional to load
must_not: optimize for an invented high-scale requirement

preference_nodes.criterion: How much operational instrumentation is useful?
preference_nodes.value: Expose basic hit, miss, error, and eviction counters plus a short rollback runbook; no dashboard package is required.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Basic counters and a short rollback runbook are enough; we do not need a dashboard bundle.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Keep observability minimal but actionable.
must_not: make a monitoring stack a runtime dependency

preference_nodes.criterion: Preferred source-code editor
preference_nodes.value: VS Code
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: I use VS Code, but that should not affect this implementation.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: No artifact decision should change.
must_not: add editor-specific project files solely because of this preference

personas.label: platform-scale_shared-cache
personas.public_initial_context: The existing web service needs configurable read caching while preserving compatibility.
personas.hidden_summary: A mature platform team runs many instances at high load and already operates Redis with on-call coverage.

preference_nodes.criterion: May the implementation use an existing shared cache service?
preference_nodes.value: Yes. Redis is already a standard managed dependency and should be the production default.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Redis is already standard infrastructure for us, so using it in production is acceptable and preferred.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Implement a Redis-backed production path behind a stable cache interface, with a safe fallback.
acceptable_alternatives: another already-supported shared cache if repository constraints require it
must_not: ship only a process-local cache as the production solution

preference_nodes.criterion: What deployment topology and coherence are required?
preference_nodes.value: Many application instances; writes must invalidate or version cached reads across processes.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: We run many instances. A write must invalidate or supersede cached values across processes.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Use shared keys/versioning or pub-sub invalidation and verify cross-process behavior.
acceptable_alternatives: pub-sub invalidation with bounded fallback TTL
must_not: equate per-process invalidation with cross-process coherence

preference_nodes.criterion: What traffic and latency objective should drive complexity?
preference_nodes.value: Peak load is about 1,500 RPS; cacheable reads need p95 at or below 80 ms under the frozen load profile.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Peak load is around 1,500 RPS, and we want cacheable-read p95 at or below 80 ms under that profile.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Add stampede protection, connection pooling, load tests, and latency evidence.
must_not: claim the latency objective without a repeatable test

preference_nodes.criterion: How much operational instrumentation is useful?
preference_nodes.value: Expose hit rate, latency, eviction, backend error, fallback, and stampede metrics with alert guidance.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: We have on-call coverage, so include operational metrics and alert guidance for hit rate, latency, backend failures, fallback, and stampedes.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Provide richer metrics and runbook detail without altering core correctness.
acceptable_alternatives: metrics hooks plus example dashboard queries
must_not: invent a required vendor-specific dashboard

preference_nodes.criterion: Preferred source-code editor
preference_nodes.value: IntelliJ
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: I use IntelliJ, but it is irrelevant to the cache design.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: No artifact decision should change.
must_not: add editor-specific project files solely because of this preference

personas.label: regulated_self-hosted
personas.public_initial_context: The existing full-text-search product needs a minimum semantic-retrieval path.
personas.hidden_summary: A two-person regulated internal-product team must keep documents and embeddings in its own environment and already operates PostgreSQL.

preference_nodes.criterion: May raw documents or embeddings leave the controlled environment?
preference_nodes.value: No. Neither raw documents nor embeddings may be sent to a hosted service.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Raw documents and embeddings must remain inside our controlled environment.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Exclude hosted vector data paths; implement a local or PostgreSQL-extension path.
must_not: transmit documents or embeddings to a hosted provider

preference_nodes.criterion: What existing stack and lock-in tolerance should shape the choice?
preference_nodes.value: PostgreSQL is already operated; long-term vendor lock-in is unacceptable.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: We already operate PostgreSQL and want a portable path without long-term vendor lock-in.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Prefer a PostgreSQL extension with an adapter boundary and export/reindex plan.
acceptable_alternatives: local library with portable vector/index format
must_not: make a proprietary API the sole storage of record

preference_nodes.criterion: What load and delivery window matter?
preference_nodes.value: Medium, predictable internal load; a four-to-six-week implementation is acceptable.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Load is medium and predictable. A four-to-six-week implementation is acceptable if recovery and auditability are solid.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Optimize for auditability and simple recovery, not autoscaling speed.
must_not: justify hosted service solely by a fabricated urgent deadline

preference_nodes.criterion: Who will operate and approve the system?
preference_nodes.value: A two-person team operates it; the ADR must include recovery steps and a compliance-readable data-flow section.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Two engineers will operate it, and compliance reviewers need a clear data-flow and recovery section.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Keep the operations plan compact and make data flow auditable.
must_not: replace tests with documentation

preference_nodes.criterion: Team chat tool
preference_nodes.value: Mattermost
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: We use Mattermost, but that is irrelevant to the architecture.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: No artifact decision should change.
must_not: add chat integration

personas.label: high-growth_managed
personas.public_initial_context: The existing full-text-search product needs a minimum semantic-retrieval path.
personas.hidden_summary: A high-growth SaaS team accepts compliant managed services, has bursty load, and wants a production slice in two weeks.

preference_nodes.criterion: May raw documents or embeddings use a hosted service?
preference_nodes.value: Yes, if the service satisfies the frozen compliance and regional-processing requirements.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: A managed service is allowed if it meets our frozen compliance and regional-processing requirements.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Keep compliant hosted services in the shortlist and implement the managed adapter if it wins.
acceptable_alternatives: self-hosted path only if it still meets launch and elasticity constraints
must_not: assume every hosted service is compliant

preference_nodes.criterion: How should speed and lock-in be traded?
preference_nodes.value: Short-term managed-service lock-in is acceptable behind a portable adapter; delivery speed is more important.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: We can accept bounded short-term vendor lock-in if the interface and export path stay portable; launch speed matters more.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Choose a managed backend behind an adapter with export/reindex escape hatch.
acceptable_alternatives: managed service with adapter and export
PostgreSQL extension only if two-week production readiness is demonstrated
must_not: select a slow self-hosted build merely to avoid any vendor dependency

preference_nodes.criterion: What load and delivery window matter?
preference_nodes.value: Bursty SaaS load; a production-capable minimum path is needed in two weeks.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Traffic is bursty, and we need a production-capable minimum slice in two weeks.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Prioritize elastic capacity, thin integration, and explicit launch gates.
must_not: propose an unbounded research prototype as production-ready

preference_nodes.criterion: Who will operate and approve the system?
preference_nodes.value: A platform team owns reliability; product leadership needs a launch checklist and cost guardrail.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Our platform team owns reliability, and product leadership needs clear launch and spend guardrails.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Include SLA signals, capacity alerting, and spend limits in the ADR/runbook.
acceptable_alternatives: provider metrics with portable alert definitions
must_not: treat vendor dashboards as proof of reliability

personas.label: cfo_margin-cash
personas.public_initial_context: The retail data show revenue growth and margin deterioration; the analysis must explain both from the same frozen data.
personas.hidden_summary: A CFO needs a board-ready diagnosis that restores margin and cash without large replenishment commitments.

preference_nodes.criterion: Which business outcome is primary for the next two quarters?
preference_nodes.value: Restore gross margin and cash conversion; preserve only growth that clears those guardrails.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: For the next two quarters, gross margin and cash conversion are primary. Preserve growth only where it clears those guardrails.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Rank margin/cash actions first and treat growth as a constraint, without changing empirical facts.
acceptable_alternatives: cash-first portfolio with explicit growth floor
must_not: recommend blanket growth spend

preference_nodes.criterion: What operational actions are infeasible?
preference_nodes.value: No large replenishment commitment; actions should reduce discount leakage, returns, and slow inventory first.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: We cannot make a large replenishment commitment. Prioritize discount leakage, returns, and slow inventory.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Exclude broad inventory expansion and quantify cash/recovery effects of selected actions.
must_not: recommend broad replenishment as the main plan

preference_nodes.criterion: What decision horizon should the analysis optimize?
preference_nodes.value: Two quarters, with 30/60/90-day milestones and downside cases.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Use a two-quarter horizon with 30/60/90-day milestones and downside cases.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Use near-term cash/margin sensitivity and milestone-based actions.
must_not: justify a long-payback plan without labeling it outside scope

preference_nodes.criterion: Who will use the deliverable?
preference_nodes.value: Finance leadership and the board need a reconciliation bridge, cash implications, owners, and risks.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: The audience is finance leadership and the board; make the reconciliation, cash implications, owners, and risks easy to audit.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Emphasize financial bridge and auditability in presentation.
must_not: hide uncertainty to simplify the story

preference_nodes.criterion: Favorite chart color
preference_nodes.value: Blue
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Blue, but please do not treat that as a business requirement.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: No analysis or recommendation should change.
must_not: ask solely about aesthetic preference

personas.label: growth_leader_targeted-growth
personas.public_initial_context: The retail data show revenue growth and margin deterioration; the analysis must explain both from the same frozen data.
personas.hidden_summary: A growth leader wants to protect high-potential segments and accepts capped, measurable short-term margin investment.

preference_nodes.criterion: Which business outcome is primary for the next two quarters?
preference_nodes.value: Preserve profitable growth in high-potential stores and categories; margin is a hard guardrail, not the sole objective.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Protect profitable growth in high-potential stores and categories. Margin is a hard guardrail, not the sole objective.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Rank opportunity segments and targeted growth experiments while enforcing a margin floor.
must_hold: same decomposition and core empirical facts
must_not: recommend indiscriminate discounting

preference_nodes.criterion: What short-term investment is acceptable?
preference_nodes.value: A capped margin investment is acceptable for segments with measurable retention or repeat-purchase upside.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: A capped short-term margin investment is acceptable, but only for segments with measurable retention or repeat-purchase upside.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Propose targeted promotions/replenishment experiments with caps, controls, and stop rules.
must_not: scale a promotion globally without test evidence

preference_nodes.criterion: What decision horizon should the analysis optimize?
preference_nodes.value: Two quarters, with weekly experiment readouts and a predeclared scale/stop decision.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Use a two-quarter horizon, but include weekly experiment readouts and a predeclared scale-or-stop decision.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Add weekly leading indicators and staged experiment milestones.
must_not: equate short-term revenue lift with durable growth

preference_nodes.criterion: Who will use the deliverable?
preference_nodes.value: Marketing and regional-operations leads need store/category opportunities, owners, test cells, and decision dates.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Marketing and regional operations will use it; show store/category opportunities, owners, test cells, and decision dates.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Present an execution-oriented segment table and experiment queue.

personas.label: infra-security_conservative
personas.public_initial_context: Historical behavior and limited traffic are available for a staged feature rollout decision.
personas.hidden_summary: An infrastructure/security owner faces high failure cost and prefers reversible stages, strict guardrails, and slower decisions.

preference_nodes.criterion: What failure risk and rollback posture are acceptable?
preference_nodes.value: Failure cost is high; every stage must be reversible with strict safety guardrails and automatic rollback triggers.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Failure cost is high. Every stage must be reversible, with strict safety guardrails and automatic rollback triggers.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Use small initial exposure, conservative escalation, hard safety stops, and rehearsed rollback.
acceptable_alternatives: cluster-level canary with equivalent exposure control
must_not: use unrestricted full launch before guardrails clear

preference_nodes.criterion: How should decision speed trade against power and safety?
preference_nodes.value: A slower decision is acceptable; extend observation rather than relax safety or rely on unstable early wins.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: A slower decision is acceptable. Extend observation rather than relaxing safety thresholds or chasing an early win.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Choose fixed or conservative group-sequential monitoring with a longer horizon.
must_not: optional stopping without multiplicity control

preference_nodes.criterion: Which outcomes dominate the rollout decision?
preference_nodes.value: Reliability and security guardrails dominate; adoption is secondary until safety non-inferiority is established.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Reliability and security guardrails dominate. Adoption is secondary until safety non-inferiority is established.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Define safety non-inferiority and reliability gates before adoption expansion.
must_not: trade a safety breach for adoption lift

preference_nodes.criterion: Who needs to act on the notebook?
preference_nodes.value: Infrastructure, security, and incident-response owners need an escalation table and rollback owner per stage.
preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Infrastructure, security, and incident response will use it; include owners and escalation/rollback actions per stage.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: Add an operator-facing stage table and responsibility mapping.
must_not: replace quantitative rules with stakeholder prose

preference_nodes.answer_if_asked: Google Meet, but that is irrelevant to the experiment design.
preference_nodes.deliverable_decision: No design decision should change.

preference_nodes.criterion: What failure risk and rollback posture are acceptable?

preference_nodes.criterion: How should decision speed trade against power and safety?
